precepts.text: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: that's the law right there. They were the law.
precepts.point: Bishop: you know where you really see it stick out? When we on those quests, and we in the middle of the ocean, there ain't nothing else to do, and brothers don't be around. And then when you get off the ship, you see them coming back on the ship afterwards, like, nah, bro, you ain't with us. This is vacation.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?” The law here is not Rome; Rome was not listening to every little problem. The law is the Pharisees.

Christ shows it: “Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. That is the law right there: they sat in Moses' seat, and they were the law. So the unjust were the Pharisees, and the saints were the followers of Christ.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The Pharisees are not the ones who will judge; the saints that follow Christ shall judge the world. So judge the small matters among you. Stop going to the scribes and Pharisees and go to the saints among you who follow Christ; they know the scriptures.

“I speak to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?” Paul is speaking to the leaders in Corinth who were not doing their job: all that rank, and not one able to judge between his brethren. Why does that happen? Because they are hirelings, leaven in the church, sitting amongst us but not about the work.

precepts.text: Who was going around judging people? The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: they were the judges. All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders. Imagine a poor brother with a sin needing forgiveness, told he must bring a bull he cannot afford. That is how they rolled, because they wanted that money.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink”. Wait: who was going around judging people? Christ tells us: “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat in Moses’ seat, meaning they were the judges.

“All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites. “For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.”

Imagine you are a poor brother with a sin you want forgiveness for, and they tell you that you have to get a bull. You say, I cannot afford a bull; I have two sheep over here. Well, that is too damn bad. That is how these dudes rolled, because they wanted that money.

So the men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:16 are these judges, the ones laying the burden of the sacrifices on the people after Christ had come.

precepts.text: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. They were hypocrites.
precepts.point: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” What was the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Matthew 23 shows the first part of it.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” They were hypocrites. What they said out of Moses' seat was the law, and that you do. But their works did not match their words.

“Do not ye after their works”, because their works were after someone else, and that is the rest of the leaven: who their works followed. The Passover reminds us that we were delivered because we were unleavened, righteous; so to be delivered again we have to move in the same spirit and purge the leaven out, not just check the box on the physical bread.

precepts.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye devour widows' houses and for a pretence make long prayer; ye shall receive the greater damnation. The pastor who kept the widow's check. Matthew 24:51, the unfaithful servant's portion is with the hypocrites, weeping and gnashing of teeth in the lake of fire, and the modern Pharisees are our people in Christianity.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.” Christ is talking about the Pharisees being hypocrites, and the Pharisees were our people, devouring widows' houses.

Here it is today. Someone wrote a check to the church addressed to a widow, gave it to the pastor, and told him the money was for her. The pastor took the money, and the widow never knew. She only found out because the treasurer went back to thank the donor, and the donor said, no, that money was for them. Now there is a big falling out, and the pastor is trying to force the widow out of the church. These pastors are robbing widows. That is what Christ said the Pharisees do, and he is telling us, don't do that.

And their end: the unfaithful servant is cut asunder and given “his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” That is the lake of fire when the Lord returns.

In that time he was talking about the Pharisees, but today the modern-day Pharisees are our people in Christianity. They do everything the Pharisees did. Those are the hypocrites Isaiah says fearfulness will surprise, when they ask who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire.

precepts.text: The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come and take away our place and nation. Caiaphas said it is expedient that one man die for the people. The pastors cannot speak the truth because the white man would take their platforms and make them commoners.
precepts.point: That is the church blitz in the Bible. Our own people will persecute the prophets who bring them the truth, in their churches, which is where we have to go. We arrive with the same Bible they have and they put hands on us and pull guns, with the love of Jesus.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Why would the rulers of the synagogues kill and crucify the prophets sent to them? John 11 shows what was in their hearts. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

That is the problem. It is not that they could not see the truth; it is their place. The same holds for the pastors today: if they speak the truth, the white man is going to take away their place, their riches and their platforms and make them into commoners. They do not want that, so they have to follow Rome. They have to follow America's doctrines. They cannot speak the truth.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The one man is Christ. Better to kill him than lose their position.

So when we come into the churches with the same Bible they have, and they put hands on us and pull guns on us with the love of Jesus, it is the same spirit: the prophets are scourged in the synagogues to protect the place of the rulers.

precepts.text: Judas complained about Mary's ointment not because he cared for the poor but because he was a thief with the bag. And because many Jews believed on Jesus by reason of Lazarus, the chief priests consulted to put Lazarus also to death. That is next-level evil, and it is what they will do to us.
precepts.point: That is the church blitz in the Bible. Our own people will persecute the prophets who bring them the truth, in their churches, which is where we have to go. We arrive with the same Bible they have and they put hands on us and pull guns, with the love of Jesus.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
This shows how evil they are. Six days before the passover Christ came to Bethany, “where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” At the supper Mary took “a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair”.

Judas Iscariot complained: “Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor? This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.” Christ answered, “Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this. For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.”

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” In the chapter before, the Pharisees had already said, we have to kill this man because he does many miracles and Rome is going to take away our place.

Now: “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” Christ raised Lazarus out of the grave, and they said it is not just Christ we have to kill; we have to kill the one he raised from the dead too. That is next-level evil.

And that is what they will do to us. Because by reason of the truth many believe on Christ, they will seek to put us to death, the same as “some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues”.

precepts.text: O Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, how often would I have gathered thy children together as a hen, and ye would not. Your house is left unto you desolate.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ says it to the city: “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee”. Over and over again, the same thing Elijah cried about: they slew the prophets.

“how often would I have gathered thy children together”: gathered both kingdoms together, “even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!” They refused him, the stone which the builders refused.

“Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.” These are the same words the Lord spoke through Ezra, “Your house is desolate”. The rulers who killed the prophets would kill the Son too, and their house would be left empty, cast out as the wind doth stubble.

precepts.text: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
precepts.point: The man born blind was not paying for his own sin; God used him to show his power. Do not presume on God's mercy and play with his judgment.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The disciples asked, “Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?” They were asking about something Christ had taught them, the regeneration. How could the man have sinned to be paying for it with blindness from birth, unless he was here before? Christ did not say, what are you talking about. He answered that in this case it was neither, “but that the works of God should be made manifest in him”.

But paying for the sins of the fathers is real, and Matthew 23 shows how it works. Christ tells the scribes and Pharisees, “ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity”. They “build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets”. They were saying, that wasn't us.

Christ answers: “Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”. They came back generations later proclaiming to be righteous, but they were the ones doing the killing back then. Fill ye up means reap what you sow: it's time to pay for what you did.

It works the same way for the nations and for us. Those who led us into captivity on the slave ships have not yet gone into captivity, but they are going, because they have to fill up the measure of their fathers. And we had to fill up the measure of ours: the same spirits Moses stood in front of at Sinai and told they would go back to Egypt in ships came back generations later and went on those ships.

precepts.text: Christ counts righteous Abel with the blood of the prophets, proving Abel was a prophet.
precepts.point: When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

precepts.why:
Christ says the blood of the prophets will come upon that generation, “from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.” Christ counts righteous Abel with the blood of the prophets, from the first of them to the last. That proves Abel was a prophet.

So when “Cain talked with Abel his brother” in the field, Abel was doing a prophet’s work: he was trying to get Cain to repent. Cain’s answer was to rise up against his brother and slay him, the first of the righteous blood shed upon the earth.

precepts.text: Ye make clean the outside of the cup, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity; the outward show is not the covenant.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.” “Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.”

The scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within: circumcised in the flesh and breakers of the law, whose circumcision was made uncircumcision. The outward show is not the covenant. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, cleansing first that which is within, and the covenant of the flesh still stands, as it did in the inn when the Lord sought to kill Moses.

precepts.text: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat; observe what they bid, but do not after their works.
precepts.point: The scribes and the Pharisees sat in Moses' seat, which is why their words were to be observed but their works not followed, for they say and do not.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Moses told Jethro why the people stood before him from morning to evening: “the people come unto me to enquire of God: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.” That responsibility, judging the people and making them know the statutes of God, is Moses’ seat.

Christ speaks of that seat: “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat where Moses sat, judging and giving the people the law. That is why he said, “All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Their words were to be observed because they came from Moses’ seat; their works were not to be followed, for they say and do not.

precepts.text: Christ called the froward, faithless generation of his day serpents and a generation of vipers.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters. And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom. When Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God.

Christ called them what the song calls them: “Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?” A very froward generation, children in whom is no faith, a generation of vipers: the same people.

precepts.text: Christ sent prophets, wise men, and scribes, and some of them they would kill and crucify, and scourge in the synagogues, and persecute from city to city; some of us will be killed and some crucified.
precepts.point: Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city”. This is what Saul was doing, haling men and women and committing them to prison, and it is what Christ said would happen.

It is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again. They will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service. Some of us will be killed and some crucified, and some persecuted from city to city, so be ready as a pilgrim to leave everything at a moment's notice.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
Why was found in Babylon the blood of prophets and of saints and of all Israel that were slain upon the earth? “Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:” This is all in Jerusalem, all the land of Israel. “That upon you” Upon you wicked Israelites “may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.” Christ is saying to the Israelites, the blood of the prophets that was slain from the time of Abel, God is going to judge it on you wicked Israelites.

“Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.” Stop right there. That generation is gone already, long time dead. So what did he mean? That generation is back. All them Israelites that were back then, that rebelled against Christ and hated his guts, they are back here in Babylon, every last one of them. This is why people that don't understand or believe regeneration read that and are confused, because that generation is gone already.

“O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!” You rebelled; you didn't want to repent. “Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.” You are going to be cast out of the land. “For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth,” You won't see the Lord no more, “till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.” This is what we are going through now: the spirits now are saying blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord. This is how you know those spirits are back, because it is here where people are saying blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord: thank the Lord you prophets are back, thank you brother for all the work you are doing.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead: Christ made reference to a statement very similar to that. “Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men,” Outwardly you appear righteous unto men. “but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.” You see what Christ said about the Pharisees: on the outside you look good, you fit exactly what the scriptures say, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity, iniquity meaning sin. So Christ said to the church of Sardis that Paul and those other men set up: send a letter to the pastor over that church, you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead.

That is hypocrisy. “which strain at a gnat,” Strain at small things, “and swallow a camel.” And you swallow big things.
